title: Quantum fluctuation relations in first-detection processes
abstract: We derive two quantum fluctuation relations for systems undergoing repeated projective measurements. These fluctuation relations characterize the work that can be extracted from a quantum device when a first-detection event triggers a mechanical operation leading to positive work production. The correction to the standard quantum Jarzynski equality depends logarithmically on the mean first-detection time for the time-reversed dynamics.   Application of Jensen's inequality leads to fundamental limits on both the total work involved in the repeated measurements and final mechanical operation, and the extracted work alone.   The general case of a device connected to an external environment is also considered.
summary: This theoretical paper develops generalized fluctuation relations for calculating work extracted from quantum devices that operate based on a first-detection trigger mechanism. It shows that these relations correct the standard Jarzynski equality by incorporating an entropic term related to the average detection time. The results establish fundamental, measurable limits on energy conversion in such measurement-driven quantum engines.
main_problem: The paper derives quantum fluctuation relations characterizing the work extractable from a quantum device undergoing repeated projective measurements triggered by a first-detection event.
main_result: Two new fluctuation relations are established, correcting the standard Jarzynski equality with an entropic term dependent on the mean first-detection time. These relations provide fundamental limits on both total and extracted work.
method: The derivation utilizes principles of quantum thermodynamics, applying Jensen's inequality to relate expectation values involving exponential functions of work, and employing time-reversal symmetry arguments.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum device subjected to repeated projective measurements (a 'quantum first-detection information engine'). The analysis considers the general case where the system interacts with an external environment.

main_assumptions: The analysis is based on the Two-Projective-Measurement (TPM) scheme, and certain normalization procedures are required if the survival probability $S_\infty[ho_{in}] > 0$.

paper_structure: The paper builds upon the standard Quantum Jarzynski Equality (QJE) by incorporating the non-Markovian effects of repeated measurements. It derives fluctuation relations for total work and extracted work, showing how these are modified by terms related to the mean first-detection time.
why_interesting: This work extends fundamental theorems like the Jarzynski equality into the regime of measurement-induced quantum engines, providing new bounds on energy extraction that depend on the measurement protocol itself. This is highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium thermodynamics in open quantum systems.
